conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Joint Board of County Commissioners and Board of Education Quarterly Meeting
conflicts.issue: FY21 County Budget Gap for DPS ($5.23M vs. $19M Request), Fund Balance Comparisons, and 2020 School Bond
conflicts.summary: DPS board members pressed county officials over the ~$15 million operating shortfall leaving $15/hour staff pay unfunded and resisted county comparisons of fund balances, while a proposal for a November 2020 bond drew county pushback.
conflicts.side_a_position: Seek deeper county operating/capital support—including exploring a modest November 2020 bond—and clarify that DPS's ~$8.3M-$11M fund balance is not comparable to the county's $62.5M unassigned ($211.1M total) reserves.
side_a_arguments: DPS's unanimous $19M request included $15/hour minimum wages for lowest-paid staff and level-funding needs (~$7M just to stay level), leaving a $15M gap.
Waiting until 2022 delays shovel-ready school projects, and DPS's small fund balance is already strained by COVID-19 expenses without net savings.
conflicts.side_b_position: Hold the FY21 increase at $5.23M ($3.2M operating, $2M capital) plus $176M in front-loaded LOBs while deferring any GO bond referendum to 2022.
side_b_arguments: A November 2020 bond would trigger an immediate property tax hike during a severe pandemic downturn, while LOBs already fund Northern High School and Elementary C.
The county carries $26M/year in existing school debt service and must preserve reserves to protect its AAA bond rating amid plunging sales taxes.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; county staff provided the FY19 unassigned fund balance figure ($62,456,569) while both boards acknowledged continuing budget uncertainty from the General Assembly.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Joint Board of County Commissioners and Board of Education Quarterly Meeting
conflicts.issue: Urgency of Joint City-County-DPS CARES Act Digital Equity Plan vs. Immediate Device Ordering
conflicts.summary: Board members and county commissioners debated whether the city, county, and DPS could quickly convene a joint task force to coordinate CARES Act funds for hotspots and devices before the June 1 filing deadline.
conflicts.side_a_position: Rapidly convene city, county, and school finance/leadership staff to align CARES Act funding on student digital access and countywide broadband.
side_a_arguments: Providing hotspots and fiber access addresses both immediate remote learning gaps and long-term rural/low-income equity across Durham.
conflicts.side_b_position: DPS cannot delay ordering devices past June 1 to wait on intergovernmental CARES negotiations, and the county's $5.48M CARES allocation faces competing small-business, food, and housing emergencies.
side_b_arguments: Global Chromebook demand requires a 60-day lead time starting before June 1, forcing DPS to front costs from fund balance first.
Durham County received only $5.48M in CARES funds compared to $11M for DPS and $194M for Wake County.
conflicts.resolution: Both boards expressed support for ongoing digital-equity collaboration between managers and Digital Durham while DPS proceeded immediately with its May 28 device procurement.

conflicts.issue: County Facility Use (Libraries) and Funding Urgency for HOPE Learning Centers
conflicts.summary: During the DPS virtual learning and budget updates, commissioners and school leaders confronted tension over whether the County could immediately open empty library facilities and commit scarce local/CARES funds for HOPE Learning Centers before September 8.
conflicts.side_a_position: Urgently assess County libraries, volunteer staff, and Round 2 CARES funds to provide free learning-center seats and digital equity for the most vulnerable students.
side_a_arguments: Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow noted the new Main Library sat empty with technology resources and directed the County Manager to return by August 24 with a facilities, staffing, and funding assessment.
BOE members (including Jovonia Lewis) stressed that 83% of DPS students are Black and brown and urged prioritizing free learning-center seats despite Community Ed shortfalls.
conflicts.side_b_position: County administration cautioned that it had not been included in initial cost projections and faced declining revenues and limited fund balance.
side_b_arguments: County Manager Wendell Davis stated County staff had not been directly involved in the HOPE Center cost numbers, noted revenue slowdowns and limited discretionary pots beyond fund balance, and committed to analyzing the $3.3 million county share of Round 2 CARES funding.
conflicts.resolution: Board directed County staff to complete a facilities, staffing, and CARES/fund-balance analysis ahead of the August 24 BOCC regular session.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education and Durham Board of County Commissioners Joint Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead presided over the November 17, 2020 joint meeting of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education and the Durham Board of County Commissioners. The two boards unanimously approved prior joint meeting minutes and the 2021 quarterly joint meeting calendar, while receiving budget and revenue updates from County Budget Director Keith Lane and DPS CFO Paul LeSieur/Alex Modesto detailing the first-year $1.9 million phase-in toward a $15/hour classified minimum wage ($14/hour in FY21) and warning of COVID-19 revenue uncertainty, $3.83 million in DPS fund balance usage, and rising learning center, connectivity, and HEPA filter expenses. DPS leadership briefed commissioners on the draft second-semester Plan B reopening framework and readiness dashboards, and Dr. Julius Monk reviewed major capital projects including Northern High School (summer 2021 construction), Elementary School F, six elementary renovations, and the planned 2022 bond/LOBS financing strategy. County and Durham Children's Initiative staff concluded with updates on the Early Childhood Action Plan and Durham Pre-K (supporting 441 local-dollar-braided seats) ahead of February 2021 budget coordination.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Review, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the joint BOE-BOCC meeting to order and confirmed no agenda changes were needed. Present BOCC Commissioners (Howerton, Jacobs, Carter) and DPS Board Members (Ravin, Beyer, Lewis, Umstead) unanimously approved the prior joint meeting minutes by roll call.

agenda_items.title: FY 2020-21 Budget Follow-Up and $15/Hour Minimum Wage Phase-In
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Budget Director Keith Lane reviewed the county's $1.9 million FY21 allocation toward a two-year phase-in of DPS's $15/hour classified wage request (bringing minimum pay to ~$14/hour, leaving $1,907,000 needed for full implementation) while cautioning that property tax and sales tax collections remained uncertain until January 2021 and county vacant positions were frozen. DPS board members and commissioners discussed whether county fund balance reserves could accelerate full $15/hour funding in January 2021 for essential pandemic workers.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Learning and Plan B Reopening Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Dr. Julie Spencer presented DPS's draft second-semester Plan B framework and upcoming weekly health and site-readiness dashboards. Commissioners praised the depth of planning and expressed commitment to supporting whichever instructional decision the school board makes.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Projects and 2022 Bond/LOBS Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk updated both boards on the $500 million 10-year capital commitment, noting Northern High School construction starts in summer 2021, Elementary School F design negotiations with a Durham minority-owned firm are underway, six elementary school renovations are in RFQ review for 2023 completion, and high school theater lighting is out for bid. Natalie Beyer pressed for a 2022 GO bond to address deferred HVAC, roof, and Jordan High School needs, and Keith Lane and county staff affirmed commitment to meeting the CIP schedule through LOBS and a planned 2022 bond referendum.

agenda_items.title: DPS COVID-19 Relief Funding, Connectivity, and Budget Risks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Paul LeSieur and Alex Modesto detailed state ADM hold-harmless protection at 33,368 students (versus 31,603 actual enrollment), CARES Act ($11.9M) and Coronavirus Relief Fund allocations expiring December 30, 2020, and looming FY22 fiscal cliffs including $2.6 million in annual hotspot connectivity and $2.5 million in annual 1:1 device refresh costs alongside $1.5 million in Learning Center deficits and $800,000 in HEPA filtration. Frederick Xavier Ravin III suggested exploring remaining CRF Wi-Fi equipment funds for community Wi-Fi extenders, and Commissioner Wendy Jacobs noted the county's northern broadband study.

agenda_items.title: Early Childhood Action Plan and Durham Pre-K Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Early Childhood Coordinator Katie Lender, DCI's David Reese, and Linda Chappelle presented progress on the county's Early Childhood Action Plan (high-level recommendations due February/March, final plan in June) and Durham Pre-K. Chappelle reported local dollars were supporting 441 braided Pre-K seats (136 fully locally funded) and expressed hope for additional state Leandro Pre-K funding.

agenda_items.title: Approval of 2021 Joint Meeting Schedule and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The boards unanimously approved the 2021 quarterly joint meeting calendar with locations pending health guidance. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs flagged that the gap between February and May meetings might require an interim budget coordination session, which Chair Umstead welcomed, and Alexandra Valladares asked the county to include DPS in future environmental and building sustainability contracts.

votes.item_title: Approval of Joint BOE-BOCC Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Joint board roll call: 4 DPS members present (Ravin, Beyer, Lewis, Umstead) voted Yes; BOCC Commissioners Jacobs and Carter (and Howerton called) voted Yes; Dr. Mike Lee, Matt Sears, and Alexandra Valladares not recorded in this early roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Bettina Umstead called the roll of present BOCC commissioners (Jacobs, Carter; Howerton noted on screen) and DPS school board members (Ravin, Beyer, Lewis, Umstead) to approve the prior joint meeting minutes.

votes.item_title: Approval of 2021 Joint BOE-BOCC Quarterly Meeting Schedule
votes.notes: Joint board roll call: DPS members Lewis, Beyer, Ravin, and Umstead voted Aye; BOCC Commissioners Jacobs, Howerton, and Carter voted Aye.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved four quarterly joint meetings for 2021 with physical or virtual locations pending health and safety guidance.

meetings.title: Joint BOCC-BOE Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the August 18, 2020 Joint Board of County Commissioners and Durham Public Schools Board of Education virtual meeting, opening with unanimous approval of the February 4 and May 19, 2020 joint minutes (5-0 BOCC; unanimous with BOE). DPS leadership briefed both boards on the launch of Plan C virtual learning, device delays tied to federal sanctions, and the urgent $3.3+ million community coalition request for HOPE Learning Centers—prompting Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow to direct County Manager Wendell Davis to assess using County libraries and staff alongside Round 2 CARES Act funds ($3.3 million county share). Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt and COO Julius Monk warned that USDA summer meal waivers would expire September 1, leaving pre-K/non-DPS and delivery gaps ahead of a proposed home-delivery contract. Both boards also reviewed Northern High School and Elementary School C construction timelines, a $3.8 million DPS COVID-19 budget gap covered from fund balance, and pre-K slot reductions alongside threats to local childcare providers, before hearing public comments backing HOPE Centers and adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval of February 4 and May 19, 2020 Joint Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs added a Durham Pre-K update before future meeting dates, and both boards voted unanimously (5-0 BOCC and unanimous BOE) by roll-call voice vote to approve the February 4 and May 19, 2020 joint meeting minutes.

agenda_items.title: Update on DPS Virtual Learning, Device Deployment, and HOPE Learning Centers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Deputy Superintendent Nakia Hardy and COO Julius Monk outlined Plan C synchronous schedules, FHI 360 social-emotional supports, Lenovo Chromebook delays caused by U.S. sanctions, and community-led HOPE Learning Centers aiming to serve 2,100+ vulnerable students. Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Reckhow expressed concern over learning loss and directed County Manager Wendell Davis to assess County libraries, staff, and Round 2 CARES Act funds ($3.3 million county share) ahead of the August 24 BOCC meeting.

agenda_items.title: School Meals and Community Food Security Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt and Dr. Monk reported that Durham Feast delivered over 500,000 meals through July 31, and warned that federal summer meal waivers expiring September 1 would restrict DPS meals to 25 school pickup sites for enrolled students only. Rewalt previewed an August 24 BOCC proposal with Food Insight Group to continue home deliveries for transportation-limited families, while BOE member Alexandra Valladares and community voices urged culturally responsive and grassroots partnerships.

agenda_items.title: Construction Update: Northern High School and Elementary School C
agenda_items.discussion_summary: New DPS Design, Construction, and Sustainability Director Frederick Davis presented renderings and schedules for Northern High School (bidding February 2021, substantial completion June 2023) and Elementary School C on Scott King Road (groundbreaking October 2020, opening August 2022, including pre-K classrooms). Chair Jacobs raised concern over NCDOT shifting off-site traffic and pedestrian safety costs onto school districts and urged close coordination so Vision Zero/Safe Routes to School safety is not compromised.

agenda_items.title: DPS FY2020–21 Budget Development and COVID-19 Fiscal Risks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS CFO Paul LeSieur and Budget Director Alex Modestou detailed state mini-budget flat pay, retirement/health cost hikes, $11.89 million in CARES Act device/connectivity funding, and a $3.8 million local COVID budget gap covered by growing fund balance from $8.3 million to ~$11 million. They warned of major risks from enrollment uncertainty, FFCRA leave without federal reimbursement, and enterprise shortfalls in Child Nutrition and Community Education as BOE members urged county help for free learning-center seats.

agenda_items.title: DPS and Durham Pre-K Enrollment Update, Future Dates, and Public Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Debbie Pittman, Suzanne Cotterman, and Linda Pell reported that social-distancing square-footage rules cut district pre-K slots, DPS waived $56,000 in first-nine-weeks Montessori/Whitted fees, and 40%–46% of licensed private childcare centers faced closure risk at half capacity. After scheduling the next joint meeting for October 20 and reading public comments urging full funding of HOPE Learning Centers, Chair Jacobs adjourned the meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of February 4 and May 19, 2020 Joint BOCC-BOE Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: BOCC voted 5-0 Aye; DPS Board of Education members present also voted Aye unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Clerk Monica Toomer called the joint roll of County Commissioners and Board of Education members to approve the February 4 and May 19, 2020 minutes.

meetings.title: Durham Joint Board of County Commissioners and Board of Education Quarterly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 19, 2020 virtual quarterly joint meeting of the Durham Board of County Commissioners and Durham Public Schools Board of Education presided over by DPS Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the boards unanimously approved the agenda and reviewed the county's revised 10-year Capital Improvement Plan—which expanded school capital allocations from $320 million to $482.5 million, including $176 million in LOBs for Northern High School and Elementary School C plus planned 2022 and 2026 GO bonds. Officials discussed transitioning the Durham Feast pandemic feeding initiative into DPS's June 8 summer feeding program, DPS's 'Growing Together' student-assignment and boundary equity plan, and DPS's urgent June 1 timeline to order 1:1 student devices using fund balance pending CARES Act funding. During the FY 2020-21 county budget presentation, DPS members Natalie Beyer, Minnie Forte-Brown, and Dr. Mike Lee pressed county officials on the ~$15 million gap between DPS's $19 million request and the manager's recommended $5.23 million increase ($3.2M operations, $2M capital) and disputed fund-balance comparisons, while Beyer floated a modest November 2020 school bond that county leaders cautioned would force tax hikes amid COVID-19 revenue losses. The meeting closed with an update on a joint city-county-DPS face-covering procurement effort bolstered by $40,000 from the city and $10,000 from DPS travel savings.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Joint Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened with a moment of silence honoring first responders and essential workers during COVID-19. After BOCC Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs requested time for a face-covering update and Steve Unruhe urged keeping items moving within the two-hour window, the joint boards approved the agenda unanimously by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Durham County and DPS Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim/Deputy County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane reported the manager's recommended FY21 budget raised DPS 10-year CIP funding from $320M to $482.5M ($176M in LOBs for Northern High School and Elementary C, planned 2022 and 2026 GO bonds, $1M/year released lottery funds, and a $2M increase in annual current capital to $3.37M alongside ~$26M/year in school debt service). Dr. Julius Monk noted Elementary C aimed to break ground in August and Northern in late fall, and confirmed Hillside High lighting was in year-one funding.

agenda_items.title: Community Feeding Program (Durham Feast) Sustainability
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff (Drew Cummings and Donna Rewalt) and Dr. Julius Monk reviewed transitioning from the DPS Foundation/Food Insight Group Durham Feast partnership to DPS's traditional 24-site summer feeding program on June 8 once staff returned from emergency leave, while the Foundation continued Wednesday home deliveries to ~1,000 vulnerable families. BOCC Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs flagged that county CARES funding would be needed to sustain adult meal support.

agenda_items.title: Growing Together: Plans for Growth, Equity, and Access
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk and School Planning Director Matthew Palmer presented DPS's 18-month 'Growing Together' student assignment, magnet, and boundary-equity framework addressing 22 of 30 elementary schools at or over capacity, ~3,000 projected students from >10,000 planned residential units, and over $500M in deferred maintenance ahead of Elementary C (2022) and F (2023). Natalie Beyer suggested a modest November 2020 bond to accelerate shovel-ready projects, which county commissioners and Claudia Hager resisted due to immediate tax impacts and LOB sequencing ahead of 2022.

agenda_items.title: DPS 1:1 Technology Plan and Joint CARES Act Coordination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni outlined DPS's $6.89M 1:1 device estimate and June 1 ordering deadline, while CFO Paul LeSieur noted DPS's ~$8.3M-$11M fund balance and June 1 CARES filing deadline (~$11M DPS vs. $5.48M county). Natalie Beyer, Bettina Umstead, and BOCC Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Heidi Carter pushed to form a joint city-county-DPS digital equity group, while Dr. Mubenga stressed DPS could not wait past June 1 to order student devices.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Updates and County Services Impact on DPS Families
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy briefly summarized DPS's Reentry Planning Task Force, three-phase instructional packet distribution, and specialty high school graduations. County General Manager Joanne Pierce and BOCC Vice Chair Jacobs detailed essential DSS, immunization, and digital library services, while Xavier Cason and Natalie Beyer urged expanding mental-health resilience and summer youth programming alongside Spanish-language outreach.

agenda_items.title: Durham County FY 2020-21 Budget Overview and Face-Covering Project Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Budget Director Keith Lane presented the FY21 recommended budget adding $5.23M for DPS ($3.2M operating, $2M capital; $151.2M direct plus $32M indirect/debt), prompting Natalie Beyer, Minnie Forte-Brown, and Dr. Mike Lee to highlight DPS's ~$15M shortfall for $15/hour wages and question county fund-balance comparisons ($62.46M unassigned / $211.1M total vs. DPS's $8.3M-$11M). Finally, BOCC Vice Chair Jacobs reported Duke physicists were evaluating masks for the joint face-covering project, backed by $40,000 from Durham and $10,000 from DPS travel funds.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 19, 2020 Joint BOE/BOCC Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Joint meeting with the Durham Board of County Commissioners; reflects the seven DPS board members voting Aye alongside participating County Commissioners.
votes.discussion_detail: A member moved and another seconded approving the joint meeting agenda (with Chair Dr. Mike Lee noting a face-covering update could be fit in if time allowed). Passed unanimously on the joint BOE/BOCC roll call.
